explanation: In 1457 an act passed under James II banned golf, so that men would practise archery for war instead. James III and James IV repeated the ban.

claims.text: In 1457 an act of the Parliament of Scotland under King James II banned golf, to protect archery practice.
Acts under James III in 1471 and James IV in 1491 repeated the ban on golf.
